title: Workspace router
blurb: Document-app launch router from manifest-incubations #141 that focuses matching notebooks in place, opens different notebooks via window.open() when activated, falls back to an in-app prompt, and guards against link-capturing loops.
question: Can a focus-existing document app route launches for a different notebook into a separate window with window.open() when activation is present, while cleanly degrading to an in-app prompt when absent?
result: On headed Chrome for Testing 153 under xvfb with popup blocking enabled, clicking Route ?doc=b opened ?doc=b&spawned=1, routing after 6 s expiry rendered the in-app prompt, and both prompt buttons ('Open it in a new window' and 'Switch this window instead') worked. Installed-app launch delivery and desktop link-capturing interaction not verified in Chrome 160.
testedIn: Headed Chrome for Testing 153 under xvfb (click and expired baselines verified); installed-app launch not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Link capturing can route an in-scope URL passed to window.open() back into the same focus-existing window unless guarded
friction.repro: From a focus-existing installed app with 'open supported links' enabled, call window.open() with an in-scope URL lacking a loop-guard query parameter.
friction.browser: Chrome desktop (unverified whether link capturing intercepts same-window window.open in Chrome 160)
friction.workaround: Append a marker parameter (such as &spawned=1) to URLs opened via window.open() and switch in place instead of spawning again if that marker arrives in launchQueue.
